claim: Digital Music News reported that of Patreon's 79,420 creators, only 1,393 — under 2% — earned the US federal monthly minimum wage of $1,160 in October 2017, and only 0.8% (635 creators) reached a $15/hour equivalent.
stance_target: The claim that only a low single-digit percentage of creators on direct-monetization platforms earn a living wage
scope_conditions: Patreon; earnings month October 2017; published 2 January 2018; derived from Graphtreon's scrape of publicly disclosed Patreon earnings, which covers roughly 80% of creators; US federal minimum wage benchmark
quoted_support: According to the website, the platform now has 79,420 creators. Yet, only 1,393 creators (under 2%) earned the federal monthly minimum wage of $1,160 a month in October 2017. Even worse, if changed to $15 per hour, only 0.8%, or 635 creators, made that amount.
region: US wage benchmark applied to a global platform — US/Western-only threshold

claim: The vast majority of Patreon creators earned between $1 and $100 per month as of late 2017, placing the modal creator's platform income at roughly one to two percent of a minimum-wage income.
stance_target: The claim that median creator platform income is negligible rather than merely low
scope_conditions: Patreon; late 2017; Graphtreon distribution of publicly disclosed earnings
quoted_support: In addition, Graphtreon found that the vast majority on the platform earned between $1 and $100 a month.

claim: Patreon reached 50,000 monthly active creators and roughly one million monthly active patrons in 2017, with estimated total creator earnings of $150 million for the year — meaning average annual earnings of about $3,000 per active creator against a median far below that.
stance_target: The claim that mean creator earnings badly misrepresent typical outcomes on skewed platforms
scope_conditions: Patreon 2017; note the tension between 50,000 monthly ACTIVE creators and the 79,420 total creator count used as the denominator for the minimum-wage statistic; the $3,000 mean is this analysis's arithmetic, not the source's
quoted_support: the service reached 50,000 monthly active content creators last year. With the support of one million monthly active patrons, the company estimated that creators would earn $150 million last year.

claim: Patreon's December 2017 service-fee change triggered mass patron cancellations and caused content creators to shut down their pages, a documented case of a unilateral platform policy change directly precipitating creator exits.
stance_target: The claim that platform policy changes are a documented cause of creator attrition independent of audience or skill
scope_conditions: Patreon, December 2017; the proposed 2.9% plus 35-cent per-pledge fee was withdrawn after backlash; no quantified count of pages closed is given
quoted_support: Following a huge wave of backlash on social media, users quickly bailed from the platform. Content creators shut down their pages after hundreds of patrons canceled their pledges.

claim: Patreon's own 2016 claim that 7,960 creators earned over $100 a month against roughly 25,000 creators — nearly one third — was contradicted by the 2017 measured distribution, and the underlying blog post was subsequently deleted or moved.
stance_target: Platform-published creator success statistics as reliable evidence
scope_conditions: Patreon 2016 versus October 2017; the thresholds differ ($100/month vs $1,160/month) so the comparison shows dilution rather than direct contradiction
quoted_support: The findings contradicted Patreon's 2016 announcement that 7,960 creators on the platform made over $100 a month. With around 25,000 creators, that would mean nearly one-third of creators made over $100. The post has since been deleted or moved.
